headline_marked: France protests: [[Nearly 1,000 arrested]] amid clashes over cost of living
headline: France protests: Nearly 1,000 arrested amid clashes over cost of living
summary: Thousands took to the streets across France to protest rising living costs and poor education conditions. Clashes erupted in several cities, leading to nearly 1,000 arrests.
details: Thousands of people across France have protested against the rising cost of living and the poor state of educational institutions, with clashes erupting in several cities. The Interior Ministry reported that approximately 1,000 individuals were arrested following the demonstrations.

While most of the day's protests remained peaceful, tensions escalated in Paris and other cities at night. Police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse demonstrators. In Marseille, protesters set fire to barricades on the street, and in Bordeaux, they dismantled wooden planks from a shop to create roadblocks.

Officials noted that this weekend's protests saw less severe rioting, looting, and vandalism compared to the previous weekend, which was described as one of the most serious incidents of disorder in recent French history. The government aimed to prevent a recurrence of last week's violence.

The French Interior Ministry estimated that around 410,000 people participated in Saturday's protests, while labor unions claimed the number was closer to 800,000. To maintain control, approximately 70,000 police officers were deployed nationwide, with special restrictions imposed in several cities.

Earlier this week, President Emmanuel Macron announced that only protests organized by recognized labor unions would be permitted. In parallel, hundreds have been sentenced to prison in recent days following swift judicial processes for charges including vandalism, arson, and looting.

In Paris, clashes began at the end of a peaceful march. Some protesters erected temporary barricades and threw objects at the police. When masked youths broke the windows of a car showroom, police intervened with batons.

A specialized police unit, typically involved in combating organized crime and terrorism, also participated in the operation. Interior Minister Gérald Darmanin stated that several thousand far-right activists had gathered, identifying about 500 of them as participants in the riots.

In Marseille, protesters set fire to trash cans and used metal sheets to block roads. A law enforcement vehicle was seen navigating through a burning barricade. In Bordeaux, masked protesters attempted to create roadblocks.

In Lyon, police used tear gas to disperse demonstrators in a prohibited area. One protester reported that their group of about 150, mostly secondary and university students, were immediately met with tear gas, significantly reducing visibility.
The Interior Minister confirmed the arrest of nearly 1,000 people, warning that the number could increase. He also reported two serious injuries, one in Toulouse and another in Clermont-Ferrand.

Protesters expressed deep frustration with the government, citing economic hardship and a lack of voice. "They silence us. They take our money, impose extra taxes, yet we can't say anything. We've endured this for too long," said one protester named Zélie. Another young protester echoed feelings of generational neglect, though condemning last week's looting as a response to poverty and police violence.

headline_marked: Dhaka ranks [[world's 5th most polluted city]] Sunday morning
headline: Dhaka ranks world's 5th most polluted city Sunday morning
summary: Air quality index (AQI) hit 173, with PM2.5 levels nearly 17 times higher than WHO annual guidelines.
details: Dhaka was ranked as the fifth most polluted city in the world on Sunday morning, according to the Switzerland-based IQAir. The city's Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 173, which is categorized as 'unhealthy'.

The primary pollutant in Dhaka's air was PM2.5, with a concentration of 88.5 micrograms per cubic meter. This level is approximately 17 times higher than the annual guidelines set by the World Health Organization (WHO).
Among Dhaka's 12 monitoring stations, Abdullahbag in North Badda recorded the highest pollution level with a score of 201, crossing the 'very unhealthy' threshold.
Other highly polluted areas in the capital include Gulshan Lake Park (186), BIDS office in Agargaon (179), Baridhara Lake Side (179), and Baridhara Park Road (177).
Outside the capital, Rajshahi recorded the highest pollution among divisional cities with a score of 169, followed by Khulna (164), Rangpur (157), and Mymensingh (155).
Other divisional cities included Barishal (151), Chattogram (142), and Sylhet (112). IQAir notes that these indices are real-time and subject to change over time.
caption:
